title: Respiratory pathogen survey reveals mixed infections in Zhuhai children - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was conducted between January 2024 and December 2025, with the report published on October 26, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on Zhuhai, China, analyzing throat-swab specimens from patients with influenza-like illness and severe acute respiratory infection. Children aged 0–14 years accounted for 96.11% of positive cases.
analysis.event: A two-year surveillance study in Zhuhai, China, found that 64.56% of 2,788 patients had respiratory pathogens, with nearly half of the positive samples containing more than one organism. The study identified 20 of 22 pathogens tested, including human adenovirus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Mixed infections were common, with 48.28% of positive samples containing multiple pathogens. The most prevalent pathogens included human adenovirus, influenza A virus, and human rhinovirus. The study noted that human adenovirus positivity was higher among males, while Mycoplasma pneumoniae was higher among females. The findings highlight the co-circulation of several respiratory pathogens in Zhuhai during the study period.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study used real-time PCR to test specimens and descriptive epidemiology to analyze the data. It emphasized that the results describe the enrolled clinical populations rather than the full population of Zhuhai. The observational design does not establish causation for any particular illness or clinical outcome.

analysis.brief_en: A two-year respiratory pathogen surveillance study in Zhuhai, China, revealed that 64.56% of 2,788 patients tested positive for pathogens, with nearly half of these cases involving mixed infections. The study, published on October 26, 2026, focused on children aged 0–14 years, who accounted for 96.11% of all positive cases. Researchers used real-time PCR to detect 20 of 22 tested pathogens, including human adenovirus, influenza A virus, and human rhinovirus. The findings indicated that mixed infections were common, with the most frequent combination involving Haemophilus influenzae. The study also noted sex-specific differences in pathogen positivity, with human rhinovirus and Haemophilus influenzae more prevalent in males, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae more common in females. However, the observational design does not establish causation for any specific illness or outcome. The results highlight the concurrent circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens in Zhuhai during 2024–2025, with notable age and seasonal patterns.

title: Same RSV antigen, two vaccine platforms, two different immune maps in mice - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was published on October 28, 2026, and the immune profiling was conducted up to 120 days after immunization. The earliest immune responses were observed 14 days after the prime immunization and continued to be monitored through day 49 and day 28 after the booster.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted on female BALB/c mice, with immune profiling carried out in the serum, spleen, bone marrow, draining lymph nodes, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.
analysis.event: A preclinical study compared two RSV vaccines using the same prefusion F antigen but different platforms: a lipid nanoparticle-formulated self-amplifying RNA vaccine and an adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine. The study found that the adenoviral vector induced systemic immunity, while the RNA vaccine induced immunity within the lungs. The event is confirmed based on the experimental results and immune profiling.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study reported that the adenoviral vaccine produced higher serum IgG titers and more IgG-positive antibody-secreting cells in the spleen, while the RNA vaccine showed higher IgG binding antibodies in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and more pronounced T-cell responses in the lung. The study did not assess protective efficacy in vivo, and the risk of vaccine-associated enhanced respiratory disease was not evaluated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was published in EMBO Molecular Medicine and conducted by researchers at Sichuan University. The findings are based on in vitro and in vivo experiments, and the authors suggest that combined saRNA-adenoviral regimens may be worth future evaluation. The study used only female BALB/c mice and the intramuscular route, leaving other delivery routes unexplored.

analysis.brief_en: A preclinical study published on October 28, 2026, in EMBO Molecular Medicine compared two respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines using the same prefusion F antigen but different platforms: a lipid nanoparticle-formulated self-amplifying RNA vaccine and an adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine. The research, conducted by Sichuan University, found that the adenoviral vaccine induced systemic immunity, while the RNA vaccine generated immunity within the lungs. Both vaccines drove detectable prefusion F protein expression in HEK293T cells, and immune profiling revealed differences in antibody and T-cell responses. The adenoviral platform showed higher serum IgG titers and more IgG-positive antibody-secreting cells in the spleen, whereas the RNA vaccine elicited higher IgG binding antibodies in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and more pronounced T-cell responses in the lung. The study did not test protective efficacy in vivo and used only female BALB/c mice with intramuscular delivery, leaving other routes unexplored. The authors suggest that combined saRNA-adenoviral regimens may be worth further investigation.
analysis.summary_en: A preclinical study published on October 28, 2026, in EMBO Molecular Medicine compared two respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines using the same prefusion F antigen but different platforms: a lipid nanoparticle-formulated self-amplifying RNA vaccine and an adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine.
